title: Évariste Galois — MacTutor History of Mathematics Archive
author: J. J. O'Connor and E. F. Robertson
whyRelevant: Primary biographical source. Hedges legends (the eraser; the all-night writing) against the documentary record. The single most reliable English-language biography online.

title: Évariste Galois — Wikipedia (English)
whyRelevant: Cross-reference for dates, names, document quotes (testament letter, banquet toast, last words to Alfred). Cross-checked May 2026.

title: Évariste Galois — Encyclopedia Britannica
whyRelevant: Concise corroboration of family background, the funeral riot, the political fuse after his father's suicide.

title: Genius and Biographers: The Fictionalization of Évariste Galois
author: Tony Rothman
venue: American Mathematical Monthly, vol. 89 no. 2, pp. 84–106
whyRelevant: The canonical debunking of the romantic Galois myth (the all-night invention, the duel-over-a-femme-fatale, E. T. Bell's purple prose). Required reading before scripting Acts 1, 6, and the criticisms section.

title: The Mathematical Writings of Évariste Galois
author: Peter M. Neumann
publisher: European Mathematical Society (Heritage of European Mathematics)
whyRelevant: Modern critical edition of Galois's manuscripts, with parallel French/English translations and notes. The authoritative source on the testament letter and the marginal annotations.

title: The Bicentennial of Évariste Galois
author: Robert Gardner
whyRelevant: Useful narrative summary with reproductions of the duel-night letter quotations. Convenient cross-check on letter texts.

title: A History of Galois Fields
author: Frédéric Brechenmacher
whyRelevant: Definitive account of the 1830 finite-field paper and how Liouville's 1846 publication interacted with the broader 19th-century group-theory tradition (Cauchy, Serret, Jordan).

title: Œuvres mathématiques d'Évariste Galois (Journal de mathématiques pures et appliquées, Tome XI, 1846, pp. 381–444)
author: Évariste Galois, edited by Joseph Liouville
whyRelevant: The original posthumous publication. The literal moment Galois's ideas reach the printed page, fourteen years after the duel.

title: Traité des substitutions et des équations algébriques
author: Camille Jordan
whyRelevant: The book that turned Galois's manuscript into a discipline. The hinge between Galois and modern group theory. Read by Klein and Lie in Paris that same summer.

title: Abel–Ruffini theorem — Wikipedia
whyRelevant: Cross-reference for the 1799 Ruffini / 1824 Abel chronology and the modern Galois-theoretic statement.

title: Solvable group — Wikipedia
whyRelevant: Standard definition of the solvable chain and the equivalence with the derived series — the core technical object of Acts 3 and 5.

title: Alternating group — Wikipedia
whyRelevant: Reference for |A_n| = n!/2, A_5 simplicity, and the icosahedral isomorphism A_5 ≅ I.

title: Galois theory — Wikipedia
whyRelevant: Modern statement of the Galois correspondence and a cross-reference for the canonical examples used in Act 3 (x^3 - 2 / Q).

title: Erlangen program — Wikipedia
whyRelevant: Cross-reference for Klein's 1872 reformulation of geometry as the study of group invariants. Anchor of the Act 7 legacy montage.

title: Noether's theorem — Wikipedia
whyRelevant: Reference for the 1918 statement and the discrete-to-continuous bridge from Galois groups to Lie groups in physics.

title: Advanced Encryption Standard — Wikipedia
whyRelevant: Confirms AES operates on bytes interpreted as elements of GF(2^8) with the irreducible polynomial x^8 + x^4 + x^3 + x + 1 — the closing flourish of Act 7.

title: Reed–Solomon error correction — Wikipedia
whyRelevant: Confirms the use of Galois fields in CDs, DVDs, QR codes, and Voyager telemetry.

title: Genius and Biographers (full PDF host on tufts.edu)
author: Tony Rothman
whyRelevant: Mirror of ref-rothman-1982 (publisher's authoritative landing page on Taylor & Francis).

title: Marie Ennemond Camille Jordan — MacTutor
whyRelevant: Confirms Klein and Lie's 1870 Paris pilgrimage to study the Traité under Jordan's guidance.

title: Felix Christian Klein — MacTutor
whyRelevant: Cross-reference for the 1870 Paris visit and the path from Jordan's Traité to the 1872 Erlangen Program.
